dialect.detail: Brazilian Portuguese COBOL subprogram, likely compiled with a Brazilian vendor compiler (possibly Unisys or similar) given 'decimal-point is comma', 'console is crt', and 'lock mode is automatic' file control clauses. Date 1992. References to 'REAIS', 'CRUZEIROS', 'BILHAO', 'MILHAO' suggest Brazilian currency context.
evidence: lock mode is automatic with lock on record

purpose.domain_detail: Brazilian currency amount-to-words (extenso) conversion utility subprogram
purpose.summary: This is a COBOL subprogram (called via PROCEDURE DIVISION USING) that converts a numeric monetary value into its written-out Portuguese text equivalent (extenso). It handles billions, millions, thousands, units, and cents in Brazilian currency (Reais/Cruzeiros), reading descriptions from an indexed file (arqext) and building the result string in a linkage section buffer.

notable_features: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING linkage section (subprogram interface)
Indexed file with LOCK MODE AUTOMATIC and WITH LOCK ON RECORD
REDEFINES on linkage value to split into 3-digit groups (link-vlr-cruz)
OCCURS clauses for character-by-character string building
No COMP-3 usage despite financial domain
verdict.notes: Source truncated at 16000 chars but all four divisions are present and the logic is clear. The program was written in 1992 in Brazil. Currency references include both 'CRUZEIROS' (old currency) and 'REAIS' (new currency introduced 1994), suggesting the code was updated or written in anticipation of the currency change. The indexed file 'arqext' stores the text descriptions for numeric values, making this a table-driven extenso converter.
